The petitioner was put to trial for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 344, 376(2)(n)
of the Indian Penal Code respectively (for short, The IPC) and Sections 5(l) and 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short, Date: 2026.04.01 16:10:01 IST Reason:
POCSO Act) respectively.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. At the end of the trial, the petitioner was held guilty of the offence with which he was charged.
The Trial Court sentenced him to undergo 20 years of rigorous imprisonment for the offence punishable under the POCSO Act.
5. Being dissatisfied with the judgment and order of conviction passed by the Trial Court, the petitioner has preferred Criminal Appeal No.1453 of 2023 in the High Court.
6. In the said appeal, the petitioner preferred an application praying for suspension of the substantive order of sentence passed by the Trial Court.
The High Court declined to suspend the substantive order sentence passed by the Trial Court.
7. In such circumstances, the petitioner is here before us with the present petition.
8. We heard Mr. Shubham Jain, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and Mr. Shiv Mangal Sharma, the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the State of Rajasthan.

9. We looked into the oral evidence on record, more particularly, the oral testimony of the victim,
her Statement before the learned Magistrate recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and other circumstances on record.
10.
We are of the view that the petitioner has been able to make out a case for suspension of the substantive order of sentence imposed by the Trial Court.
11. We do not propose to observe anything further as Criminal Appeal is pending before the High Court.

12. The substantive order of sentence passed by the Trial Court in Sessions Case No.54/2021 decided by the Special Judge (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012) and Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, No.-1, Ajmer, Rajasthan shall remain suspended and the petitioner is ordered to be released on bail, subject to terms and conditions that the Trial Court may deem fit to impose.

14. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
(VISHAL ANAND) (POOJA SHARMA)
